values: Honesty; uphold and defend the truth at all times
Justice and fairness in dealing with others
Integrity; moral uprightness and sound character

themes.theme_description: Focus on personal relationships, family, and home life.

topics.core_competency: The learner appreciates families and the vocabulary related to family relationships and descriptions.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: pronounce, listen to, read and write the Local Language (k, s).
differentiate between Local Language alphabet and the English alphabet (u).
use vowel length (s).
describe family genealogy and relationships (k, u).
write numerals (k, s, gs)
write days of the week, months of the year and dates (k, u, s)
write time (k, u).
welcome, greet and bid farewell using appropriate vocabulary (words) while observing time, number, gender and age of people (k, v).
use gestures that accompany greeting to express respect, age difference/similarity and so on (s, gs).
write informal letters (k, s, gs).
use riddles related to family (k, v).

suggested_learning_activities.description: learner illustrates the English language alphabet on the board.
the teacher guides the learner to identify, list and pronounce letters of the local language alphabet from a given text.
learner populates the generated list of sounds/letters with relevant examples of words from the text studied.
learner constructs additional words outside the given text that contain specific sounds.
teacher engages learner in a spelling exercise by dictating specific words especially those with common confusing sounds such as dh and th, ng and ŋ and those with diacritic marks.
teacher brainstorms with learners about members in their families.
teacher draws an example of a family tree on the board.
through discussion, teacher asks learner to study a family tree chart and asks them to state any reasons for its arrangement.
teacher then wraps up the discussion.
using the given example of a family in (2), learners draw family trees reflecting their own immediate family genealogies.
as an individual project, teacher may ask learners to generate a larger relational tree of their families and clans.
teacher asks learners in groups to read a short text of a half-page containing numbers 1-20 in words.
teacher asks learners to write numbers 1-20 in figures and words.
teacher explains common rules observed in writing numbers beyond 20 in words.
using the principles learnt, learners write numbers beyond 20 in words (21-1,000,000)
teacher asks learners to mention their position of birth in family.
teacher asks learners to line up and mention their positions in the line.
teacher provides learners with flashcards containing ordinal numbers 1-20.
using examples in flashcards, learners write ordinal numbers 21-1000.
teacher asks learners what day of the week it is.
learners read aloud a poem about days of the week and corresponding activities.
teacher asks learners to write days of the week and their activities from the poem.
teacher presents learners with a table of months of the year in the local language.
learners match months of the year in English and the local language.

teacher demonstrates how to write dates in a local language e.g. 03/12/1454. Ka adek dwe marapar g’aryo oro ma gana achiel pyer’apar dingwen gi pyer’abich g’angwen (Dhopadhola); Nga isatu omwezi gwa Namuwawuzo, mu mwaka lukumi bina ataanu n’ena(Lusoga); Eraasi auni olap loka Orara okaru loka ilukumit akwata aungon akaisiakany aungon (Ateso).
teacher points key prepositions, conjunctions and punctuations involved in writing date e.g. ‘on’.
teacher asks learners to write their personal birthdays and those of three family members.
teacher asks learners to divide and name parts of the day: dawn, morning, noon, afternoon, evening and night in the local language.
teacher guides learner to group times of the day into morning, afternoon, evening and night e.g. 12am-11am (morning), 12pm-3pm (afternoon), 4pm-7pm (evening), 8pm-11pm (night).

through group discussion, the teacher asks learners to write equivalents of specific terms such as am, pm, second, minute, hour, time, half-past, quarter-past or quarter-to, break, lunch, dinner, supper, etc. in the local language.
teacher illustrates to learners how to write given time in the local language in words or figures e.g. 10:15am (Sawa angwen gi dakika apar g’abich m’odikini); saawa inhha ne dakiika ikumi na itanu.
teacher asks learners to pair up and greet one another.
teacher asks one learner to greet a group of learners.
learner greets the teacher.
teacher asks learners to talk about/explain what rules they followed while greeting in scenarios 1-3.
teacher clarifies or sums up rules involved in greeting (time, number, gender, title, and age).
teacher guides learners to construct a greeting dialogue.
teacher asks learners to discuss and demonstrate how they would greet peers, in-laws, women, men, and elders.
teacher engages learners to critique the greeting demonstrations and clarifies on some gestures.
teacher asks learners to comment on the greeting gestures from other cultures vis-a-viz their own.
teacher asks learners to mention types of letters they know.
teacher asks learners to identify examples of people to whom informal letters can be written.
teacher demonstrates on the board or presents a text example of an informal letter.
teacher asks learners to study example in 3 and identify parts of the letter.
teacher guides learners to write their own letters to a family member, friend or relative.
teacher begins the lesson by giving examples of riddles and learners respond.
teacher groups learners and tasks them to write ten riddles.
learners share their collections with the rest of the class.
after sharing, teacher asks learners to suggest importance of riddles.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: compares Local Language and English language alphabets.
spells words from a dictation.
transcribes words recorded in an electronic device.
tabulates words according to vowel length e.g. bana vs baana, baba vs baaba, etc.
writes a greeting dialogue with two responses for each time variation, that is, morning, afternoon and evening.
responds to questions from an audio or audio-visual recorded greeting dialogue.
writes given figures in the local language using words e.g. 14,579.
writes a letter to a relative.
poses and responds to five riddles related to family.
draws an extended family tree.

project_requirements.project_scope_verbatim: as an individual project, teacher may ask learners to generate a larger relational tree of their families and clans.

suggested_uses: use recorded episodes to support development of listening and speaking skills.

topics.core_competency: The learner understands the home environment and the roles of the people at home.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: tell roles of different people at home (k, u).
appreciate members of the family for carrying out their roles efficiently using appropriate vocabulary (v, a).
appreciate the values of lullabies at home (k, v).
name objects found at home in singular and plural (k, u).
identify how some traditional objects, crafts and wears are made (k, u).
explain the importance of domestic objects and wears (k, v).
appreciate traditional fashion and style (k, v)
appreciate the taboos related to the misuse of some of the objects at home (v, a).

suggested_learning_activities.description: teacher probes learner to name titles of different people at home.
through a discussion, the teacher asks earners to describe the roles of people at home.
in their groups learners generate lists of common words related to roles played in a home.
learners engage in a conversation using common words used in a family.
teacher provides a text on appreciation.
learners identify the words/ language used in appreciation
learners share life examples/ personal experiences of appreciation/gratitude.
in groups, learners explain the purpose/benefits of appreciation and effects of ingratitude.
learner writes a letter of appreciation to a family member for help received.
teacher probes learners to mention various songs sung in their community and their purpose.
the teacher picks out a lullaby and explains what it is.
the learners sing the lullabies they know from their communities.
in their groups learners compose lullabies.
leaners present their composed lullabies.
teacher provides a text with plural and singular forms of objects found at home.
learners identify objects they have at their homes.
the learners generate a table of singular and plural forms of objects at home
teacher guides learners to identify some traditional objects, crafts or wears and describe how they are made.
teacher sums-up the process of making any given traditional object, craft or wear e.g. mortar/pestle, sieve, rope, mat, footwear or backcloth.
learners write a half-page composition describing how any chosen traditional object, wear or craft is made.
in groups, learners discuss the importance of any traditional object or wear.
learners present their group’s finding in a plenary.
teacher guides learners to appreciate the concept of moral and physical beauty.

with vivid examples, teacher guides learners to discover aspects of moral beauty of a person in a traditional setting (honesty, appropriate language, respect of rule of law and order, respect for elders, hard work, etc.)
in groups, learners discuss aspects of physical beauty of a person in a traditional setting (decency, adornment, grooming, tooth extraction, body size, traditional dress codes, etc.)
using specific examples, teacher guides learners to understand the meaning of ‘taboo’.
in groups, learners identify and discuss the purpose of taboos associated with misuse of some objects found in a home.
learners share their findings in a plenary.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: debates on topics related to the family such as: ‘Mother is more important to the family than Father.’
writes the singular and plural of objects found at home.
writes a letter of apology or of gratitude to a family member.
writes a lullaby, rehearses it and discusses its importance.
makes a traditional object such as a banana fibre ball or skipping rope.
writes a one-page essay describing how one traditional object is made.
debates on traditional beauty vs modern beauty.
picks a role model from each side of beauty and explain why they admire them.

explains the rationale of at least five taboos associated with misuse of some traditional objects/crafts/wares. e.g Not sitting on the mortar is for hygiene purposes i.e. the mortar is used for preparing food and therefore should be kept clean/not be contaminated.
identifies at least five proverbs associated with the taboos on misuse of those objects /crafts/wares.
writes a short essay on the roles of people at home (100-150 words).

practicals.title: Make a traditional object
practicals.description_verbatim: makes a traditional object such as a banana fibre ball or skipping rope.

suggested_uses: use the Internet to obtain images or digital camera to take pictures of the objects in a home to support class discussion.
Use a computer to prepare a list of tribes and their cultural dress codes (where applicable).

themes.theme_description: Focus on occupations, farming, and food practices.

topic_metadata.topic_title: 1.3 Crops, Plants and Foods in Our Area

topics.core_competency: The learner understands knowledge concerning practices of growing crops, plants and making food.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: categorise food crops, non-food crops and wild plants and understand their importance to the family/ community (k, u, v).
differentiate seasons of the year and understand their impact on agricultural activities (k, u, v).
use appropriate vocabulary in the Local Language during planting and harvesting (k).
study the taboos related to crop growing, harvesting and seasons and how they affect the crops (k, v, a).
identify the techniques used in improving crop yields (k, v).
describe the process of food preparation (k, v).
describe ways of preserving and storing crops and food (k, v).
describe a food menu (k, u).
use a dictionary (k, u, s, gs).

suggested_learning_activities.description: teacher groups learners and asks them to identify examples of food crops, non-food crops and wild plants in the community.
teacher guides learners to discuss the importance of crops and wild plants to the community.
learners write one-page composition describing the importance of crops.
learners study a text on different seasons and their impact on agricultural activities.
learners identify seasons mentioned in the text and their respective activities.
learners identify impacts of the season on the activities.
teacher guides learners to understand how their community categorises seasons e.g. by weather patterns or activity.
learners in their groups discuss and identify activities carried out in particular seasons and why.
learners share experiences of how they grow and harvest any crop at home or school.
teacher provides a descriptive text on the process of growing and harvesting any chosen crop.
teacher guides learners to brainstorm on certain terms and processes as indicated in the text.
learners write a one-page description of the steps involved in growing and harvesting any crop.
teacher introduces the concept of taboos by asking learners to brainstorm the purposes of rules and regulations at school.
teacher asks learners to relate school rules and regulations to taboos involved in growing and harvesting crops.
teacher asks learners to research and report on taboos related to growing and harvesting crops in their communities.
teacher asks learners to talk about what crops were grown in their communities in their previous season and whether the yields were good or not.
teacher asks learners to explain what could have caused better or poor yields.
in groups, learners discuss methods of improving crop yields.
in their groups, teacher asks to categorise methods into traditional and modern practices.
teacher asks learners to mention various types of foods, sauces and beverages prepared at their homes.
teacher groups learners and allocates them different types of foods and asks them to describe the process involved in preparing such a food.
learners make a report on (2) above.
teacher asks learners to brainstorm on what takes place at mealtime.
in groups, teacher asks learners to identify examples of good and bad manners portrayed while having a meal.
teacher asks learners to identify the methods of food preservation or storage.
in groups, teacher tasks learners to identify the types of food and how they can be preserved or stored.
in groups, teacher provides learners with manilla papers and asks them to draw any type of food preservation or storage system known to them.
in their groups, learners present their work.
learners brainstorm on what foods, sauces and beverages they often have for a meal at home.
the class visits any local restaurant to appreciate how a food menu is prepared.
while in the field, learners take notes.
in groups, teacher asks learners to write a food menu using their field notes.
in groups, teacher provides learners with a dictionary or photocopies and guides them to locate certain words.
learners pronounce words they have located and use them to construct different sentences.
in their groups, learners display their sentences on charts.
with specific examples, teacher illustrates the meanings of synonyms, antonyms and homophones.
learners complete assignments on synonyms, antonyms and homophones.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: reads and answers questions from a comprehension passage on effects of seasonal changes on crops.
mentions five advantages of growing crops to the family/ community.
holds a debate on different topics related to agriculture such as modern vs traditional techniques of farming, advantages and disadvantages of farming, etc.
writes two taboos related to crops.
uses a graphic organiser/ template to communicate the process of preparing a favourite food.
prepares and acts a skit to educate people about table manners etiquette.
correctly pronounces particular words on a given list.
explains meanings of given words.
re-arranges given words in alphabetical order.
using minimal pairs differentiates meanings of homophones.

investigative_skills.text_verbatim: teacher asks learners to research and report on taboos related to growing and harvesting crops in their communities.

suggested_uses: use a Word processor to prepare a food menu.
use a digital camera to take pictures of local crops.

themes.theme_description: Focus on animal husbandry and care.

topics.core_competency: The learner appreciates knowledge concerning practices of animal rearing.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: name domestic animals, birds, their products and understand their importance (k, u, v).
differentiate punctuation marks and their functions (k, u).
explain taboos related to domestic animals and poultry (v, a).
identify the symptoms and traditional ways of treating some common sicknesses that affect animals (k, u, v, a).
know animal rights (k, u, v).
explain the relationship between animals and different communities in Uganda (k, u, v, a).

suggested_learning_activities.description: teacher asks learners to mention animals and birds they know.
in their groups, the learners generate a list of domestic animals, birds, their young ones and shelter.
the learners share lists.
learners discuss the importance of domestic animals and poultry.
learners research and report on ways in which domestic animals and birds contribute to livelihoods.
by way of tabulation, learners identify animals/birds and their young ones.
teacher provides a varied-punctuated text for the learner to read.
the learner identifies the different punctuation marks used in the text.
learner writes them in their local language.
learner compares them with those in the standard orthography.
leaners discuss the use/importance of each of them.
learner punctuates a given text.
teacher asks learners to identify taboos related to domestic animals and poultry.
in two groups: one for domestic animals and the second for poultry, learners discuss the taboos.
each group reports their findings.
learner writes an essay on the taboos.
teacher provides a text on animal/bird diseases.
learner describes symptoms of different diseases.
learner generates a table on animal and poultry diseases and their traditional treatment.
teacher provides a text on animal rights for learners to study.
learners identify two animal and poultry rights.
learners share their opinions/feelings on animal rights.
in their groups, learners write a composition on animal rights.
teacher guides learners to brainstorm on animals found in their communities.
learners discuss the uses of animals in different communities.
learners describe agricultural activities relating to animal rearing.
learners debate on the relationship between animals and people.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: reads/listens to a text on a topic related to health issues of animals and/or birds and answers questions.
writes a letter to his/her father informing him of the state of the animals or poultry at home.
writes a composition on the importance of domestic animals and poultry (half-page).
discusses the importance of observing the rights of animals.
reads a one-paragraph passage on the importance of domestic animals and punctuates it correctly.
fills a table with names of five animals, their young ones and shelter.
debates on topics related to birds and animals e.g. “poultry keeping is better than animal rearing.”

investigative_skills.text_verbatim: learners research and report on ways in which domestic animals and birds contribute to livelihoods.

suggested_uses: use a Word processor to generate a list of domestic animals, their young ones and shelter.
use the Internet to obtain images of domestic animals.
generate a table on animal and poultry diseases and their treatment.

themes.theme_description: Focus on personal health, hygiene, and community sanitation.

topics.core_competency: The learner understands language related to should be able to basic hygiene.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: use words related to hygiene and how it is maintained at personal and community level (k, u, v, gs).
name internal and external parts of the body that are prone to disease due to poor hygiene (k, u).
translate words and short sentences (k, s).
maintain personal hygiene and proper sanitation (gs).
explain how to prevent various diseases using traditional approaches and modern methods k, u).
compose and write simple songs and poems (s).

suggested_learning_activities.description: learners study a text on personal and community hygiene.
teacher guides learners to identify words related to hygiene from the text.
learners brainstorm the meanings of words identified.
learners use the words identified to construct sentences.
teacher groups learners, provides them with charts and asks them to draw and label the human body.
in their groups, learners identify parts of the body that are prone to disease.
learners identify different diseases that affect internal and external parts of the human body.
in groups, teacher provides learners with translated text on parts of the body and human diseases.
in their groups, learners translate short sentences related to parts of the body and human diseases into the local language.
teacher assesses learners’ work.
teacher identifies some simple songs from different languages about health and tasks learners to translate them.
learners brainstorm the different ways on how proper hygiene and sanitation are maintained.
learners discuss advantages of maintaining proper hygiene and dangers of poor hygiene.
in groups, teacher asks learners to recap various human diseases.
in their groups, learners suggest ways of preventing and treating diseases mentioned.
teacher guides learners to categorise the prevention and treatments into traditional and modern methods.
learners study sample poems/songs.
teacher recites a poem and learners sing a song along with teacher.
in groups, learners compose poems and songs about hygiene.
learners sing the songs or perform their poems.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: discusses the causes of diseases related to poor hygiene in their community.
suggests ways of preventing common diseases in the community.
draws and labels the human body.
matches six diseases related to hygiene and the body parts they attack.
writes four paragraphs about keeping their bodies and environment clean, observing the rules of orthography.
composes simple songs and poems.

suggested_uses: use electronic devices to record plays/songs/poems in a Local Language.
use mobile thermometer, stethoscope and sphygmomanometer (Blood Pressure Machine) for measuring one’s body temperature, breathing and pressure.
